transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been feeling deeply depressed, sad, and just completely empty inside for the past nine months. It feels like I'm constantly carrying this heavy weight, and I just can't seem to shake it off. I really don't know what to do anymore.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or did they come on without a clear trigger? If there was a stressor, what was it?

I'm really not sure, to be honest. I can't think of any specific stressful event or major life change that triggered all of this. It feels like these feelings just started out of nowhere without a clear cause.
Before these past nine months, had you been feeling down or depressed most days for at least two years, even if it was milder? Or did this begin as a new episode nine months ago?
No, I didn't have any long-term or milder depression before this. It definitely started as a completely new episode about nine months ago.
Have you also lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy? If so, has that been happening most days during these past nine months?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in all the hobbies and activities I used to love, and absolutely nothing brings me joy anymore. This has been happening pretty much every single day for the entire nine months.
During this time, have you had changes in sleep, appetite or weight, energy, concentration, or feelings of worthlessness or guilt?

I haven't really noticed changes in my sleep, appetite, concentration, or felt any worthlessness or guilt. However, during my high periods, I get this massive surge in both physical and mental energy where I feel like I can't stay still and always need to keep moving.

During those high periods, have you ever gone at least a week needing much less sleep and feeling unusually confident or impulsive, to the point that it caused major problems, hospitalization, or losing touch with reality? Or were the highs shorter and less severe than that?

Those high periods actually lasted for about eight months, during which I felt incredibly confident and made some very impulsive, risky decisions. I'm not sure about needing less sleep, but it never got to

During that eight-month high period, did your behavior cause severe impairment, like losing a job, major financial or legal trouble, needing hospitalization, or having psychotic symptoms such as hallucinations or delusions?

I didn't require hospitalization, but I ended up in severe financial distress due to reckless spending and making some really foolish business investments. I also had grandiose thoughts back then, truly believing I was a highly important person with a special mission.

Have you ever had hallucinations or fixed false beliefs that lasted for at least two weeks when you were not in a high or depressed mood? Or did those psychotic symptoms only happen during the mood episodes?
No, I've never experienced those kinds of false beliefs or hallucinations when my mood was normal. They only happened during that high period I went through.
During that high period, besides the grandiose beliefs, did you have any hallucinations or other delusions, or were the grandiose beliefs the only psychotic symptoms?

Yes, those grandiose beliefs were the only things I experienced. I truly believed I was a very special person with a unique mission, but I didn't have any other delusions or any hallucinations at all.
During these past nine months of depression, have you had thoughts of wanting to die, hurting yourself, or suicide?

Yes, I have struggled with those thoughts a lot during this depression. It started with just wishing I wouldn't wake up, but it has progressed to active thoughts of killing myself, sudden impulses, and I've even made specific plans and attempted to end my life.
